correctness.rationale: A scalar-scaled 2x2 unitary matrix decomposes into symmetric and skew parts, with the symmetric part having constant singular value by the SU(2) trace/Cayley-Hamilton identity. Takagi factorization and unitarity reduce it by unitary congruence to the real aI+bJ canonical form. The overlap <Ax,x> realizes exactly every m in [0,a]. For each m, y=conj(q)x+s exp(i phi)v yields an exact two-amplitude circle; optimization over m gives the sharp radii and equality thresholds, including t=0,1 and a=0,b=0. Checked random unitary decomposition and independently executed finite canonical boundary tests; numerical evidence is supplementary.

value.rationale: An explicit parameter-complete annulus formula for the simplest nonconjugate antiunitary family answers a natural two-vector numerical-range question left at implicit extrema in the closest literature. Two independently defined threshold conditions, which coincide when the symmetric and skew magnitudes agree, separate disappearance of a hole and loss of full-norm attainment; both are operator-congruence invariants with meaningful exceptional and boundary cases. This is a natural complete classification, not a recomputation of the known annulus topology or pure-skew example.
